message:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

I wanted to check how the brand work was progressing. I sent you an invitation for the landing page job and saw that you acknowledged it. I did not see a subsequent proposal, which is fine. Since we have previously discussed the website, would you prefer that I simply send you an offer? If so, would you suggest handling it hourly or at a fixed price? Based on that choice, we will need to agree either on a rate and time estimate or on a price.

A couple of job-related matters are priorities:

1\. I urgently need some kind of landing page with a sign-up button so I can establish "used in business." That will allow me to submit a trademark application and obtain a DUNS number.

2\. I am implementing the UI/UX and need to settle the layout and style of the UI shell. I have attached screenshots of a quick PoC built with the target development stack to illustrate what I have in mind.

Thanks,
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002], I’m continuing to work on the brand guide and need another day to complete it. I could put that on hold and begin the landing page instead. Would you prefer that approach?

For the landing page, I submitted a proposal at an hourly rate of $75. Would that work for you?

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001], Apologies for not responding yesterday. I was attending my granddaughter's middle school graduation at Yu Ming.

I saw that you need to do some additional work before completing the brand guide. My suggestion is that we first spend a little time exploring how the existing styles might translate to the SaaS UI and, to a lesser degree, the website. That would help me continue development and could reveal design choices to incorporate into the final guide.

Regarding the next "landing page plus" job, an hourly arrangement feels somewhat open ended while I am operating in bootstrapped mode, though I am eager for us to build an ongoing design partnership. For this particular job, could we set a fixed price of $1,000 and evaluate how that goes?

Without getting ahead of our discussions or any UI design decisions, I have attached a Google Workspace UI example to show the level of UI design quality—or better—that I would like us to target.

Please tell me whether this sounds acceptable, and I will hire you for the next job. Assuming you agree, I think it would be useful to have an early review meeting. We could meet at the office again, or hold it by video.

Best,
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]

Congratulations to your granddaughter on finishing middle school! That is such a meaningful occasion.

Based on the examples you sent, I understand that you want both the website landing page and the web app UI/UX included in one project. Could we set the landing page at $500 and use my hourly rate for the web app? I am reluctant to lock both into a fixed price because I do not yet know the scope of the web app.
And yes, I’d be glad to schedule another meeting so we can kick everything off!

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001], That works. I'll hire you to create the landing page, and we can talk through the UI/UX when we meet.

I probably did not explain the second part clearly. At this stage, I am not asking for very much: only that we agree on and style the primary UI shell elements—the header, side navigation panel, and footer—including fonts, colors, icon styles, and so on, in both light and dark modes. Screens for settings, monitoring logs, provisioning, applications, etc. will sit within the main canvas and develop over time. Their styling is a separate matter, though a very important one.

[FREELANCER_NAME_002]

Thank you for both sending the offer and providing more background on the UI/UX! (I had assumed you needed designs for Agent, Apps, and Connect.)

I’ll begin developing several landing-page layout options.

For our kick-off meeting, I’m free Mon, 6/1 from 3-5pm, and Tues, 6/2 from 11am - 4pm. Would either of those times suit you?
That works. Monday at around 4:15pm would suit me, since I need to collect my granddaughter from school at 3:15pm.
Perfect! I’ll see you tomorrow at 4:15pm.

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001], I believe the attached copy is nearly the final landing-page version, together with a few sycophantic remarks from Google Gemini ;-). I also asked some AI's about the color palette and included their answers for us to review together. [FREELANCER_NAME_002]
Thank you for sending this! I’m looking forward to talking it through later!

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001], It was good meeting with you again. Just FYI, this is the website for my other company \[[URL_001]\], which I am putting on the back burner while I concentrate on launching Actia. The site was built the old-fashioned way. Please do not allow its design to shape your work, although it is perfectly adequate for its intended market. [FREELANCER_NAME_002]

It was great meeting with you again too! Afterward, I had some trouble with my car: the battery died, and I needed to call AAA. Thankfully, the car is running again now.

iPass seems like an interesting product! It is certainly relevant in the current era of 2FA. Thank you for showing it to me!

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002], I’ve begun experimenting with ideas for the landing page’s hero section. I created two designs, each with two variations. I wanted you to see each option with both a new font (Plus Jakarta Sans) and the brand font (Alan Sans).

[URL_002]

What are your thoughts?

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001], Thank you—these are very interesting. I’m not going to respond in detail tonight because I would like to spend some time considering them and give you more useful feedback tomorrow. [FREELANCER_NAME_002]
No problem! Take your time.

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],
Here is an overview of my feedback:
\* I strongly prefer examples 1 and 2 to 3 and 4.
\* I like the landing page in "dark mode." It feels technical yet sophisticated, and the purple background you made for 1 and 2 looks excellent.
\* Emphasizing the hero text’s first sentence is very effective and works better than highlighting the tag line.
\* Alan Sans looks good to me, particularly in the headline. It comes across as warmer and more accessible (now they've got me at it!).
\* To my surprise, green works well as the button color.
\* I am undecided between the single-color and two-color versions of the logo.
\* I am unsure whether the screens are a place holder, but they may be an interesting direction to investigate.
\* Were you imagining that the remainder of the initial copy would be added to the landing page, or placed on follow-on pages?
\* Are you intending to include a shared page footer?
I look forward to seeing your next updates.
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]

Thanks for the feedback! I’m pleased that concepts 1 and 2 came out on top :)

I also agree that the first sentence is stronger than the tagline in the hero. It provides more detail, and I think it draws users in.

Yes, the blank screens are only placeholders at the moment. I can produce a straightforward mock-up that will work for releasing the page, and it can be replaced easily after the product UI has been developed further.

There is not enough copy to justify dividing the site across multiple pages, so all content will remain on the landing page. The top navigation will take users directly to particular sections of that page.

Next, I’ll use concept 1 to design the rest of the page, footer included. The neon "pulse" color will remain limited to the most important CTAs. I’ll retain Alan Sans for headers and apply Plus Jakarta Sans to all body copy.

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002]! The full landing-page mock-up is ready for you to review. A few things to note:
\- Every header uses Alan Sans
\- I incorporated some light imagery across the site
\- There is a contact form at the bottom of the page; please tell me whether you want it retained or removed
\- I created a simple footer because I do not yet know which information you want there, and I’m happy to revise it as necessary

I’m looking forward to your feedback!

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001], Thank you for this. I’ll review it and return with feedback asap.

On a separate track, I have been investigating how to code your designs for the live website. I want to build it using Claude (chat), which handles most of my work. After uploading your landing page, I explored several possible approaches. We concluded (forgive the anthropomorphism) that the site should use plain HTML with Tailwind and that Astro should be dropped, since it offers no advantage for our situation.

We also felt it would be helpful to document methods that could simplify implementation and produce a result closer to your designs. I attached a couple of short documents covering that. They are only discussion drafts at this point. Let us ;-) know your thoughts. [FREELANCER_NAME_002]
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002], since everything has already been created in Figma, handing it off to claude should be straightforward! If you prefer, I can code the page for you as well.

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001], I’ve now reviewed the complete landing-page example you sent. Seeing it in full has made me think that the follow-on copy I supplied is not suitable for the landing page, although your designs inspired some very useful ideas. I believe **How it Works** should come immediately after the opening hero section. Once a prospect is interested, that is likely to be the next information they want. Your chevron-down icons suit this perfectly because they communicate a sequence, perhaps along these lines:

**How it Works**

\* Register by providing your company information and identifying an account administrator
\* Supply background information about the company, such as by scanning its website
\* Build an agent around a business role, then give it a name and choose a voice
\* If desired, connect the agent to one of our collaborative applications
\* Provide the agent with instructions, which can be revised at any time
\* Set up a company email address for the agent and grant access authorization
\* Invite employees to use the dashboard for chatting and messaging with the agent
\* Link a switchboard extension to the agent’s phone
\* The agent is then ready to be introduced and begin working

I will have additional comments, but I wanted to send this while the idea was still fresh. [FREELANCER_NAME_002]

That reasoning makes sense! For first-time visitors, I agree that a "How it Works" section would be more useful.

When you’ve gathered all your edits, I’ll proceed with the revisions. Updating the copy should be fast, and creating the mobile-view will also be very easy because I designed the page layout to be responsive from the outset!

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

Apologies for being out of touch for several days; I have been focused on development in preparation for launch. I would now like to return to the website, since it will obviously be an integral component. The areas I want us to review and plan are:

1\. completing the assets and layout for the original landing-page design, including responsive behavior

2\. establishing the foundation for additional website pages—for example, whether they will share headers and footers, remain in "dark mode," or use a complementary "light mode" treatment (not a switchable one)

3\. determining what general guidance and/or rules we can establish for responsive behavior

4\. designing the layout and visual styling for the dashboard shell and "canvas"

FYI, I attached screens from the secure signup and login process that uses AWS Cognito. They currently rely on the AWS default appearance, although many self-styling options are available.

Some of these items belong within the existing job, while others are beyond its scope. What approach would you recommend? Should we arrange an in-person meeting or a video call to go over them?

[FREELANCER_NAME_002]

No problem whatsoever!

1\. Is there any further landing-page feedback or copy you want to change? If not, I can proceed with the revisions from your previous message

2\. Every webpage will use the same header and footer and will preserve the landing page’s dark theme

3\. We can apply the breakpoint guidance you shared earlier

4\. Could you send a screenshot showing the current dashboard and canvas? I think we could include this in the existing project by adding another milestone

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

I’m sorry—I have been extremely busy, but the website has now become my top priority:
1\. I might send a few minor copy revisions soon, but the upper half of the landing page is excellent, so let’s begin with that.
2\. agreed
3\. ok
4\. the attached Prototype UI demonstrates a functioning dashboard containing an app (agent chat). The dashboard uses its own specialized build process. At this point, I only need styling guidance for the shell container. Adding another milestone is fine.

I have settled on the website build approach, which is explained in the attached documents. Your feedback would be welcome and appreciated.

Best,
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]

To begin, Claude is requesting the following:
Token sheet — colors (hex, with bg/text/border/accent usage), type scale (family/weight/size/line-height/tracking per style), spacing scale, radii + border widths.
Font files — the .woff2 files, along with the exact family names and the weights that are actually in use.
Confirmed max content width — a single number so the precise container cap can be set.
Would it make sense to revise the brand guide document so that it covers some of these items?

I have just applied the build approach to make a framework for a website provisioning wizard. The attached skeleton page seems to work well and accommodates portrait mode. Claude would like the following visual guidance:

\* Type scale — sizes/weights/line-heights/tracking. The current headings and body settings are estimates, and the fonts will continue falling back to the system defaults until the Alan Sans + Plus Jakarta Sans .woff2 files are available.
\* Active-node accent — a decision is still needed between Signal purple and Pulse green (the one open design call).
\* Derived values to confirm or substitute: the canvas surface colour (--surface), muted text tone (--text-muted), the soft hairline (--line-soft), and the node glow.
\* Wizard-specific placeholders: --page-x (the % page margins), --wizard-panel-w (340px), --wiz-node-size, plus the portrait/landscape gaps.
\* Button states — Back/Next still lack hover/active styling because that depends on the states sheet. The current chevron is my temporary SVG pending delivery of the actual chevron asset.

I’ll continue implementing the real steps and platform interaction, so this is not blocking progress.

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002]! Apologies for replying late. I'm spending today helping my parents move out of their house, which means I won't be able to use my laptop before tomorrow. Do you have a figma account? If you do, using the figma mcp would be the simplest option! If not, I can export all the materials tomorrow.
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001], That’s completely fine, so there is no need to rush. I’m currently handling the underlying plumbing, meaning this is not holding anything up for me. [FREELANCER_NAME_002]
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002], I’ve finished the revised desktop and mobile design—here it is!

The key change is that I removed the top navigation and footer links. Because the landing page is relatively short, linking directly to individual sections is unnecessary. One question: would you like pricing information added? Alternatively, perhaps the bottom form could include a line telling visitors to contact us for pricing?
I’m currently exporting the assets, and once everything is prepared, I’ll send you a zip file.
Here is the landing-page zip! It contains all styling needed for the desktop, tablet, and mobile versions. Please let me know whether everything looks good.
For the moment, the dashboard image is only a placeholder. I intend to work on its styling next, but I did not want that work to delay the website.

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],
Thank you for providing all of the deliverables. I’ll review them soon and respond with feedback asap, although realistically that will probably not happen until tomorrow.
Best,
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]
That’s no problem—enjoy your weekend!

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002], this is the general-user flow I’ve developed:

1\. **Log in** to Actia AI
2\. **Land on dashboard** and view the agent overview
3\. **Tap "Create new agent"**
4\. **Select a business role** by choosing from Actia Roles (pre-trained templates)
5\. **Name the agent + choose a voice**, previewing the available voices before confirmation
6\. **Add instructions**, which remain editable at any time after the agent is created
7\. **Connect to an Actia App** (optional), providing a place for staff and agents to collaborate on work
8\. **Set up agent email + connect integrations** by granting email authorization through Actia Connect
9\. **Connect a phone extension** by allocating a switchboard extension to the agent
10\. **Review agent setup** and verify the name, role, voice, channels, and instructions
11\. **Agent is live** and prepared to work through phone, chat, email, and messaging

To make sure I understand correctly, you only need designs for step 1 and 11, right? Specifically, the login page and the dashboard as it appears after the user has already set up their agent?

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],
I’ve started working from the website designs you sent and wanted to confirm that our understanding is the same.
I have the example landing-page layouts for desktop and mobile. I will likely return with questions and suggestions for minor adjustments, but they provide an excellent starting point. I intend to code the first landing page from those layouts. I also received your zip file (from Figma?), which I’ll use to obtain the assets.

In parallel, I am building self-service provisioning wizards that users will access through the website, and I’ll send those to you for feedback. I also want to style the dashboard "shell" asap so that I can work on its built-in screens and loadable applications, although completing the first landing page will come first.

Please let me know whether this plan sounds right or whether I have overlooked anything.
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001], my mistake—please disregard my last message. I now understand that the zip includes a complete landing page. I’ll explore it and then send feedback. [FREELANCER_NAME_002]

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

I hope you had a good weekend. I’ve been developing your landing page design and deployed it to S3 behind CloudFront. The URL is [URL_003]. I added more copy and made several small adjustments, and I think it’s coming together really well. Let me know your thoughts.

I’ve also implemented a working tenant dashboard sign-in, although it still needs Actia branding. I’m halfway through the sign-up wizard and will add it once it’s fully functional. May I send you an invitation for an Actia login so you can review both? Tell me which email address I should use, or whether you’d like me to create an [URL_004] email for you.

I agree with your choice to remove the header navigation. Over time, I’ll put links in the footer instead, since that appears to be the current trend. I saved a few footer examples to see how others were handling them.

Best,
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002]! My weekend has been good—I went to a friend's housewarming party and also attended a concert. How has yours been?

The website looks good so far! I’ll be able to check it on a desktop later today.

Either email option is fine with me. An [URL_004] domain works if that’s your preference, or you can use my personal email, steph@stephwongstudio.com.
By the way, I'll be on a camping trip and OOO this mon - tues
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002], I’ve put together my feedback here
The sign in page looks good as well! If you want, I can create a different image to serve as the background for that page
I’m leaving for my camping trip, so I won’t be on my laptop again until tomorrow evening. Thanks!
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002]! How are things going? I’m back now from my camping trip
Please tell me if there’s anything you need

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001], Did you have a good camping trip? I hope it was fun. I received your proposed landing page edits and will apply them as soon as possible. I had tightened the spacing between sections to promote scrolling, but I’ll open it up a little more.

I’d like to set up access for you so that you can review the dashboard UI and give styling feedback. I’ll handle that as soon as I’m able and notify you when it’s ready. We should likely either create a new project or add a milestone for this work. Let me know which option you’d rather use.

Best, [FREELANCER_NAME_002]
The camping trip was great! I traveled north to Salt Point State Park
And yes, we can add another milestone for the dashboard UI

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

Great pictures! I have a couple of website items I’d like to go over with you. I want to expand the footer with additional content and the following menu links. A solid footer background using the Frequency brand color might look good.

LH block:
Actia AI (or logo)
Emeryville
California, USA
[EMAIL_001]
([PHONE_001]

RH block (links):
Home
Contact Us
Support
Cookie Notice
Privacy Policy
Terms of Use
Legal

Bottom center:
Social icons - LinkedIn, X (for now)
Copyright (c) 2026 Actia LLC. All rights reserved

I’d also like to create some informational (non-marketing) pages, including the Sign In page and an Account Provisioning wizard. They only require a background, a header logo, and possibly the footer described above. To style the AWS Cognito authentication pages, I quickly made one using your landing page background.

Best, [FREELANCER_NAME_002]

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002], 

That’s no problem—I’ll have time tomorrow to update the footer and create the backgrounds.

Happy father's day!

Steph

Thanks [FREELANCER_NAME_001], I’ve included a zip of the website in its current state. I still haven’t applied all of your updates. I added a mid-resolution breakpoint at the bottom of styles.css, which resolves the problem with the hero text and image overlapping. On my laptop, it displays much better now. I also changed the background image assets to .jpg, reducing their file size without, in my opinion, compromizing how they display. [FREELANCER_NAME_002]

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002], thank you for adding the new milestone—that arrangement works for me!

One question: was it you who sent an AWS email address verification to [EMAIL_002]?
Attached is the landing page with its revised footer. The second attachment shows the mobile version of the footer. What are your thoughts?
Would you like me to code the Sign In page and the Account Provisioning wizard page as well?
FYI, I’ll be traveling in Spain from 6/27 - 7/10. I plan to take my laptop so I can be available if anything urgent arises
If you’re happy with these, I can implement the code for it! Should I also create the additional Sign In and Account Provisioning pages?

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],
Yes, I’m currently working on AWS authentication so that you can access the Actia Dashboard/Shell. It’s running in a development sandbox at the moment, and recipient verification is required before it can send emails beyond [URL_004]. That is most likely what you received. Once you accept/verify it, I’ll be able to send your login invitation.
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]
Understood! I’ve just finished verifying my email

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001], Thank you for the footer examples. I like the layouts, but after seeing the purple color in place—even though I know I proposed it—it feels somewhat too dominant for a footer. I replaced it with a dark gray that I believe works better. What’s your opinion? [FREELANCER_NAME_002]
Yes, I agree—it works better!
What’s the best way for us to stay synchronized? Would you rather send me your edits and additions for the HTML/CSS files, or modify the latest files I provided and return the changed versions to me?
Do you use github for the website? If it suits you, I can commit straight to the repo! Otherwise, I’ll make the updates and send the revised files to you

TL/DR; just send me the files ;-)
I don’t use github in the cloud because I’ve never trusted it, even before Microsoft. Given the compromises that happen almost every day, I don’t understand why anyone uses it. On top of that, MS puts everything into its AI models. I imagine it’s now too deeply embedded in the ecosystem to replace easily.
Okay!
Attached are the files containing the revised desktop and mobile footers! Rather than the grey, I found a nice dark purple to use. Tell me what you think

Should I work on coding the additional pages next?

FYI - I’ll be traveling to Spain from 6/27 - 7/10. I’ll bring my laptop and can respond if anything urgent comes up!

That sounds wonderful! Which part are you visiting?
I also have a UI/UX design issue I’d like your perspective on. The shell/dashboard includes a collapsible panel that currently appears on the left. Certain apps may have their own collapsible panel, which is also on the left in this example. I was thinking that when both panels are present—the shell panel and the app panel—they could appear and collapse on opposite sides of the screen. First, what do you think of that approach, and second, which panel should be placed on each side? I’m leaning toward putting the shell panel on the right. I may build prototypes of both arrangements so we can test them. I’d welcome any thoughts.
It would be great if you could rough out some code for those additional pages.
I’m traveling to Spain to attend a friend’s wedding!
If it’s possible, I think the panel items should be nested beneath the applicable menu item within the same side panel instead of using multiple side panels
What content needs to appear on the Sign In page and the Provisioning Wizard page?

That’s an interesting perspective \[sic\]. People’s attention naturally returns to the left hand side, at least in the western world. Having panels on both sides may feel somewhat unnatural.

AWS Cognito generates the Sign In page, although its styling can be customized. That is why I made the background. If you visit [URL_003] and select Sign In, you’ll see what I’m referring to. I’m reusing that background for the Provisioning Wizard. Its functionality is working, but I need to revisit the styling. I’ll send it over, though probably not for a couple of days. For now, the various standard pages, such as Cookie and Privacy, are PDFs that I can simply open in another tab.
Yes, I agree that placing panels on both sides would make them compete visually. Let me know whether nesting the menu within the side panel works! If not, I can explore some other approaches
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002]! This is the design I developed for the sign in page. What are your thoughts?

Thank you for this. I’ll gather some opinions and feedback. I also wanted your thoughts about the color, shape, and size of the buttons in the shell, which I’ll refer to as Console from now on. They haven’t been styled yet, so they currently use the default: fairly large, rounded-corner buttons in a blue shade. Should we choose a color, or would monochrome be better? I’m also considering adding an icon to every button to make them more interesting.

For the Console buttons, I think using one of the brand colors would be a good choice. In terms of shape, the existing rectangle with rounded corners works well, though I can also experiment with the more rounded, pill shaped buttons used on the landing page. In my opinion, a pill shaped button would fit the brand look/feel more closely!
Could you send me a screenshot showing the current Console? I’ll use it as the starting point for designing the branded UI

Here are a couple of screens showing the light and dark theme. Tell me if you need any others. I’ve been reviewing other people’s consoles, including chatbots, upwork, RingCentral, etc. A lot of them use mono buttons.
By the way, I like the purple footer.

Thanks! I have enough now to begin.

I'm happy to hear the purple footer has gone over so well!
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002] - please review this UI for the Console when you have a chance and share any feedback you may have. Thanks!

Thanks, [FREELANCER_NAME_003] review it and follow up with my feedback. Before you leave, could you send me your proposed Sign In file? Enjoy your trip to Spain. Be sure to take some sun block and a hat ;-). [FREELANCER_NAME_002]
This is the background image for the Sign In page!
Thanks! I'm packing at the moment haha!
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002], how is everything going? I'm back from Spain and wanted to check whether you had any feedback on the designs. Thank you!

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

It's good to hear from you, and I hope your trip to Spain was fun! I've been putting a lot of work into both the website and the UI, and they are coming together quite well. My current priority is to finish fleshing out the website before it (hopefully) receives a lot of traffic.

I've added a header menu to the site that is not live yet, together with its associated pages, which are at varying stages of completion. As shown in the attached snapshots, two of these pages contain solution descriptions for the platform and agents. Each page has space for a diagram, and I have produced rough drafts for them.

I'm hoping you can help turn these drafts into production versions that I can put on the site. If you cannot, perhaps you can recommend the best way to approach this.

I've also continued developing the UI, which I'm now calling the Console, and have added further functionality. I've finalized a look-and-feel and layout that I'm comfortable with, although the shades and tones still need a little polishing. I'll send you a link that you can use to review it.

Regards,
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]

Spain was fantastic! The food was delicious, and the local history was very interesting, though it's nice to be back!

Yes, I'd be happy to help make both of these diagrams production ready.
\- For the first diagram, would you like additional customer labels for "call", "email" and "text chat"? What are the 3 other staff icons meant to represent?
\- For the second diagram, should I include directional arrows around the cycle? I'm assuming the arrows should run clockwise

Would it make sense to move to an hourly contract at this point?

That sounds good. I'm comfortable switching to an hourly contract for work like this. I can probably make that change within our current contract. What rate should I use? At this point, I just need to keep expenses under control.
If it improves the diagram, you can add "phone", "email" and "message" labels to customers, and "chat", "message" and "report" labels to staff. Yes, the second diagram should have clockwise direction arrows added.

Great! I think using hourly will be the simplest option. Would $65/hr work?

I also didn't see a 3rd milestone for the Console UI added to the contract. Do you want to add that milestone now, or should I bill that work hourly later on?

I should be able to send the new diagrams tomorrow or Tuesday.

Thank you!

Okay, I'll check whether I can switch the contract. It would be simplest if you could bill the Console UI hourly. Tomorrow or Tuesday works for the diagrams and will allow me to update the site with the menu and new pages.
I'm unsure whether upwork allows a set-rate contract to be changed to hourly within the same project. Hopefully it works! Once everything is squared away, I can send the diagrams over
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002]! Since we've moved onto the hourly one, I think we can close out this contract
